clues.title: Plate: all white or EU style, yellow taxis
text: Greek licence plates are either **all white** or have the **standard European design**, with a blue strip on the left side. Taxis have yellow licence plates.
clues.summary: Plates are either all white or the standard European style with a blue strip on the left. Taxis have yellow plates.

clues.title: Language: unique rounded alphabet
text: The Greek language features a **unique alphabet** not used in any other language. It shares similarities with both the Latin and [Cyrillic](/images/greece/greece_cyrillic.png) alphabets, however the lower case letters generally have softer shapes than the Cyrillic letters.
NOTE: Cyprus also uses the Greek alphabet.
clues.summary: A unique alphabet with softer lowercase letters than Cyrillic. Cyprus also uses it, but drives on the left.

clues.title: Pole: tall dark brown wood
text: Greek utility poles are primarily **wooden**, and often have a distinctly **dark brown** colour. They will often be noticeably taller than in other countries.
clues.summary: Utility poles are mostly wooden, often dark brown and noticeably taller than elsewhere.

clues.title: Pole: harp-shaped metal top
text: These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a **harp**.
NOTE: They are unique to Greece and Cyprus.
clues.summary: Pole tops with a metal frame shaped roughly like a harp. Only found here and in Cyprus.

clues.title: Pole: five vertical insulators
text: Many poles in Greece will have **five vertical insulators**. They can either be attached to the pole or the metal frames from the previous tip.
clues.summary: Many poles carry five upright insulators, attached either to the pole or to the metal frame of the previous top.

clues.title: Pole: side lamp with round shade
text: This type of small lamp, attached to the side of poles with a **round shade** above the light bulb.

NOTE: You can also find them in [North Macedonia](https://www.google.com/maps/@41.0299962,21.3274281,3a,26.3y,154.39h,135.54t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sU2VaxXf6zLbEjBwWs3ffLQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656) and [Serbia](https://goo.gl/maps/VbPpwagrgE3j4Y5r9).
clues.summary: A small lamp on the side of the pole with a round shade above the bulb. North Macedonia and Serbia have it too.

clues.title: Road lines: faded solid white double middle
text: In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, **solid white double middle lines**. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
clues.summary: Slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This separates it from most other Mediterranean countries.

clues.title: Road lines: yellow lines
text: **Yellow road lines** are more common in Greece than any other southern European country.
clues.summary: Yellow road lines are more common here than in any other southern European country.

clues.title: Bollard: wedge shape, squarish reflectors
text: Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with **almost square reflectors**, being red on the front and white on the back.
clues.summary: Wedge-shaped bollard with almost square reflectors, red on the front and white on the back.

clues.title: Chevron: white arrows on black
text: Greek chevrons have **white arrows** on a **black background**.
NOTE: Similar chevrons are found in Albania, Italy and the UK. Spain has the same colours, but will almost always have either two or four arrows.
clues.summary: White arrows on a black background. Albania, Italy and the UK use similar ones. Spain has the same colours but almost always two or four arrows.

differs.how: Spanish chevrons have two or four arrows

clues.title: Sign: warning sign, red border, yellow fill
text: Greek warning signs have a red border and a **yellow background**.
clues.summary: Warning signs have a red border and a yellow background.

clues.title: Sign: blue arrow signs, yellow local text
text: Greek directional signs are typically blue and arrow shaped. One of the most recognisable features are the place names, which are written in Greek with a **yellow font**, and in English with a white font.
clues.summary: Blue arrow-shaped direction signs. Place names are in Greek letters in yellow and in English in white.

clues.title: Sign: town entry, blue bars top and bottom
text: Greek town entry signs are white with thick **horizontal blue stripes** at the top and bottom.
clues.summary: Town entry signs are white with thick horizontal blue stripes at the top and bottom.

clues.title: Marker: blue km post, two alphabets
text: Greek kilometre markers are blue, having “km” written on the left in both the **Latin and Greek** alphabets.
clues.summary: Blue kilometre markers with 'km' on the left written in both Latin and Greek letters.

clues.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, two dotted lines
text: Pedestrian signs have **two dotted horizontal lines**, rather than vertical stripes.
clues.summary: Pedestrian crossing signs show two dotted horizontal lines rather than vertical stripes.

clues.title: Roadside: miniature churches on pedestals
text: These types of **miniature churches**, put on small pedestals, are often found along Greek roads and are unique to Greece.
clues.summary: Tiny churches on small pedestals often stand by the road, and are unique to this country.

clues.title: Houses: white and pastel, orange roofs
text: Greek architecture shares a lot of features with other Mediterranean countries: a lot of white and pastel-coloured stone houses with orange tiled roofs. **White houses** are very common when compared to most other Mediterranean countries.
Urban residential buildings will generally be multi-floored, light-coloured and typically have connected balconies along one or multiple walls.
Perhaps the most recognisable style of Greek architecture are the white houses with blue fences, window frames and doors. Beware that these are mainly found on islands.
clues.summary: White and pastel stone houses with orange tile roofs, with more white than in most Mediterranean countries. City blocks are multi-storey with linked balconies. White-and-blue houses are mainly on islands.

clues.title: Landscape: very mountainous, winding roads
text: Greece is a very mountainous country, with a large portion of the coverage being taken on **winding mountain roads**.
clues.summary: Very mountainous, and much of the coverage is on winding mountain roads.

clues.title: Soil: red dirt
text: **Red dirt** is very common in Greece.
NOTE: Albania also has a lot of red dirt.
clues.summary: Red dirt is very common. Albania also has a lot of it.

clues.title: Google car: low Gen 4 'smallcam'
text: Greece has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
clues.summary: Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be fully see-through.

clues.title: Coverage: bleak Gen 3 winter and autumn
text: Greece has a lot of **Generation 3 winter and fall** coverage, which tends to look somewhat bleak and depressing.
clues.summary: Lots of Gen 3 coverage taken in winter and autumn, looking bleak and grey.

clues.title: Coverage: many islands, not all covered
text: Greece is a country with many small islands, some with coverage and some without. Furthermore, while mainland Greece and Crete have all three camera generations, this will not be true for most islands.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Many small islands, some with coverage and some without. The mainland and the biggest island have all three camera generations, most other islands do not.

clues.title: Phone numbers: area code starts with 2
text: Greek **area codes** will always begin with a 2, followed by 1-3 digits determining the area.
NOTE: If the third digit is 1, you will be in the largest city of the region, and if the third digit is 9, you will be in the area surrounding that city.
clues.summary: Area codes always begin with 2, followed by 1 to 3 digits for the area. A third digit of 1 means the region's biggest city, 9 means the area around it.

clues.title: Landscape: big flat farm valleys, north
text: The largest **flat agricultural valleys** in Greece are found close to Thessaloniki and Larissa, but smaller flat valleys, where the mountains generally appear closer, can be found in several other areas in the north and centre of the country.
clues.summary: The largest flat farming valleys are near the two big northern cities. Smaller flat valleys, with mountains looking closer, appear elsewhere in the north and centre.

clues.title: Landscape: tallest mountains in the west
text: The **tallest** Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.
clues.summary: The tallest mountains are in the western half and hold most of the high mountain roads with coverage.

clues.title: Houses: all white with blue doors and shutters
text: One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture; houses with completely **white walls, blue doors** **and shutters**, is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.
clues.summary: Completely white houses with blue doors and shutters, mainly on the small central islands.

clues.title: Landscape: barren island, bushes no trees
text: On many of the central islands you can find a very **barren landscape**, with small bushes and no trees in sight. This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.
clues.summary: Many central islands are barren, with small bushes and no trees. Most common on the smaller islands with coverage.

clues.title: Plants: olive plantations, coast and south
text: **Olive plantations** are found in coastal areas, particularly on Crete and southern Peloponnese.
clues.summary: Olive groves along the coast, especially on the big southern island and in the southern part of the southern peninsula.

clues.title: Plants: citrus plantations on the south coast
text: **Citrus plantations** are mainly found in coastal areas, particularly on southern Peloponnese.
clues.summary: Citrus groves along the coast, especially in the south of the southern peninsula.

clues.title: Google car: antenna with slight bulge at tip
text: On Crete, you may find this unique car antenna, with a **slight bulge** at the tip.
clues.summary: On the big southern island you may see a car antenna with a slight bulge at its tip.

clues.title: Landscape: lone mountain south of a flat valley
text: Mount Pangaion can be recognised from its shape, being more of a **solitary mountain** rather than a wide mountain range, combined with the fact that it is located to the **south** of a flat agricultural valley.
clues.summary: A single solitary mountain, not a range, sitting south of a flat farming valley.

clues.title: Landscape: tall rock pillars with monasteries
text: These extraordinary **monolithic mountains** are called Meteora, and can be found north of Trikala.
clues.summary: Extraordinary monolithic rock towers (Meteora), found north of Trikala.

clues.title: Taxis: yellow with a blue stripe
text: **Yellow taxis** are found in Athens.
clues.summary: Yellow taxis, with a blue stripe around the car, are found in the capital.

clues.title: Taxis: blue with white roof
text: **Blue taxis** with a **white roof** are found in Thessaloniki.
clues.summary: Blue taxis with a white roof are found in the second city, in the north.

clues.title: Skyline: many very tall rooftop antennas
text: In Thessaloniki, you will often see a **large amount** of **unusually tall antennas** on top of buildings.
clues.summary: In the northern big city you often see lots of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.

clues.title: Sign: detailed pedestrian figure, no hat
text: **Horizontal Zebra stripe**: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > **Detailed guy with no hat**: Greece. Note that Greece's icon has hair that may almost look like a hat but it's just hair. Kinda looks like the Dame Tu Cosita guy

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Several countries have horizontal stripes on pedestrian signs. Here the figure is detailed and hatless. The hair can look like a hat but is just hair.

differs.how: Poland's sign is a single continuous line

clues.title: Pole: wooden crossbar top
text: In Greece you will finde a lot of these wooden crossbar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Many poles end in a wooden crossbar at the top.

clues.title: Street sign: extra panel under the name
text: Athens has this street sign with an extra part under the main street sign.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The capital's street signs have an extra panel under the main street name.
